audit.whatIsWrong: content win[] and full phases[].side both gave Gwen levels 3, 4-5 and first item, contradicting whys[2], whys[3] and whys[5], which describe free chip every wave and no way to close the gap.
audit.why: Avengerang (850 range) out-ranges Gwen's 450 Snip Snip! cone and Heroic Swing resets the gap; Gwen has no answer until two items. The 46.72% win rate matches the pessimistic prose, not the optimistic chart.
audit.corrected: Skill / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Akshan / Gwen.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early spike was built on an unverifiable Heroic Swing charge count and named no cooldowns.
audit.why: Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1 and Comeuppance 100/85/70. Those are the numbers that make 'step up now' or 'do not step up' a decision rather than a mood.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text and wants.you[0] now key the step-up to Heroic Swing's 18s rank-1 cooldown; whys[1] drops the charge claim.

audit.whatIsWrong: Nothing stated why Hallowed Mist does so little here, and Comeuppance's projectile nature was never used.
audit.why: Hallowed Mist only protects Gwen from enemies outside it, and Akshan never enters - so the mist's untargetability is dead value against a champion who wins at 850 range. Comeuppance fires projectiles that terrain and body-blocking interrupt, which is why standing behind the wave matters.
audit.corrected: early and whys[2] now state that the mist is dead value against a kiter who refuses to enter it, and that Avengerang's 850 range beats your 450 cone.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Akshan must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Full kit online, but Avengerang's 850 range beats your 450 cone. Farm the tip and wait for a Heroic Swing to go on cooldown.

edits.before: Riftmaker is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Heroic Swing's cooldown.
edits.after: His chip lands before Riftmaker does — farm, and only step up on Heroic Swing's 18s cooldown.

edits.before: Akshan's worst window — with only one Heroic Swing charge banked he can't kite far, so step up with a Q snip into an E on-hit and reset out before his Avengerang poke adds up.
edits.after: Akshan's thinnest window — Heroic Swing is 18s at rank 1, so once he spends it he cannot kite far: step up with a Q snip into an E on-hit and reset out before his Avengerang poke adds up.

edits.before: Punish levels 2-3 while he has only one Heroic Swing charge — Q snip into E on-hit, then back before Avengerang chip stacks
edits.after: Punish the 18s window right after he spends Heroic Swing — Q snip into E on-hit, then back before Avengerang chip stacks

edits.before: He banks a second Heroic Swing charge and starts grappling your Q-E poke over walls — your E reset means nothing if you can't touch him to trigger it.
edits.after: He starts grappling your Q-E poke over walls with Heroic Swing, and your E cooldown refund means nothing if you cannot touch him to trigger it.

edits.before: His Avengerang out-ranges your whole kit and you still have no W untargetability to negate it, so you eat free chip every wave.
edits.after: Avengerang's 850 range beats your 450 cone, and Hallowed Mist is dead value against a kiter who never walks into it — free chip every wave.

edits.before: Akshan is one of the few ranged tops with an actually weak early — at levels 1-2 he has only one Heroic Swing charge, so he can't kite far and that's your cleanest window. Step up with a Q snip and E in for a quick on-hit before he can chip you with Avengerang, then back out — your passive %-HP autos chunk even his low HP bar fast. The problem starts once his Swing comes online: he'll grapple back over a wall whenever you commit, and his Avengerang out-ranges everything you have until you're in melee. Don't shove into his minions chasing a Q he can just walk around — last-hit safe and accept you're behind until 6.
edits.after: Akshan is one of the few ranged tops with an actually weak early — Heroic Swing is an 18s cooldown at rank 1, so the moment he spends it he cannot kite far and that is your cleanest window. Step up with a Q snip and E in for a quick on-hit before he can chip you with Avengerang, then back out — your passive %-HP autos chunk even his low HP bar fast. The rest of the time he grapples over a wall whenever you commit, his Avengerang out-ranges everything you have, and Hallowed Mist only shields you from enemies outside it — which is a kiter's whole plan, so the mist buys almost nothing. Last-hit safe and accept you are behind until two items.

notes: The page repeatedly claims Akshan 'has only one Heroic Swing charge' at levels 1-3 and that a second charge arrives later. Riot's kit data gives Heroic Swing a flat 18/16.5/15/13.5/12s cooldown with no charge system, and nothing in the kit file supports a charge mechanic - I could not verify it, so I replaced the charge framing with the real rank-1 cooldown, which carries the same advice ('step up while Swing is down') on a fact I can stand behind. Flagged in unverified. Level chart also disagreed between the two layers and with the prose; whys[1] through whys[5] all describe an Akshan-favoured lane and the 46.72% win rate agrees, so both layers now read Skill/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Akshan/Gwen. Note spikes[0] previously called levels 2-3 'Akshan's worst window' while whys[1] and whys[2] called the same levels his - that internal contradiction is resolved in his favour. Suspect name 'Snip Snip' is a false positive.
